editorial:
Imagine taking a relaxing late-night boat trip through New York City, only to have it turn into a complete nightmare. You follow a group of friends who think they are in for a chill ride, but things go south fast when a tiny, mischievous mouse transforms into a giant, bloodthirsty monster. The vibe is a wild mix of scary and silly, making it feel like one of those B-movies that just knows how to have a good time without taking itself too seriously. It starts off slow, but once the chaos kicks in, you will be glued to your seat wondering how a cartoonish character became such a threat.

What really works here is how the movie balances the jokes with the gore. The acting feels natural, and the pacing keeps you moving from one scare to the next. While some of the monster effects might look a bit cheap to some, it actually adds to the charm of the horror-comedy style. If you are into creature features, you should definitely check this out. It looks great streaming in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, but if you are a collector, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is the way to go for the best picture quality.
endingExplained: In the final showdown, the survivors realize the monster is driven by a hunger for revenge. After a brutal fight on the deck of the boat, the main character manages to trap the giant mouse in a heavy cargo net and ignite a fuel leak. The blast blows the creature to pieces, ending the nightmare. The movie wraps up with a small hint that not all the offspring survived, leaving the door open for a sequel.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves creature features and dark humor.
